name: NBS quartz frequency-reference group
description: A group of quartz oscillators served as a United States national frequency reference.

impact.note: One laboratory's set of oscillators serving one country's radio services as a steadier reference; succeeded by improved national standards.

date.basis: Source-reported date for this scoped event.

events.statement: A group of quartz oscillators formed part of the U.S. national frequency reference from 1929.

evidence.supports: Dates the national reference group to 1929–1950 and describes its oscillator arrangement.
Identifies the group as a U.S. national reference in the NIST historical image.

evidence.locator: pp. 42–43, NBS frequency measurements and 1929 reference
evidence.supports: Describes the NBS frequency standards effort and the U.S. national quartz reference by 1929.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest documented event for this scoped record, not a claim of worldwide priority.

research.note: Independent parent inspected the cited publisher, museum, BIPM or NIST/PTB passages. Dates retain their event scope; no global priority is inferred.

caveats: The source dates the reference group, not the invention of the quartz oscillator. The count of oscillators and later replacement are not generalized to all years.
